payload.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

ambiguities: Whether the answer expects a unique maximizing x or allows multiple x values that all achieve the same maximal value
Whether the maximal value is to be expressed as a function of n (since n is a parameter)
Whether “maximal” is intended as ‘maximum value attained’ (argmax exists) rather than only ‘largest possible value’ in an infimum/supremum sense if not attained
If the maximizing set depends on n, the statement does not specify whether the dependence should be described case-by-case
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: floor(t) means the greatest integer less than or equal to t, for real t
the problem assumes the maximum over all real x exists and is attainable (not just a supremum)
the expression is interpreted for each fixed n using the finite sum over integer k from 1 to n
since the summand includes division by k, it is assumed k is nonzero; this is satisfied by k in 1..n

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
k is an integer index with 1 <= k <= n inside the sum
x ranges over all real numbers
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix any integer n with n > 1. Define f_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum from k=1 to n of (floor(k x) divided by k). Determine the real number(s) x where f_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and give the corresponding maximum value.
quantifier_order: for each integer n with n > 1
choose real x to maximize the expression over all real x

variables.name: x
variables.role: optimization variable (argument of floors and sum)

witness_dependencies: the maximizing real number(s) x* (or argmax set) may depend on n
the maximal value M may depend on n
